title: A formally verified counterexample to a continuum Fisher welfare statement
claim: A two-buyer Pareto-optimal allocation on a compact one-dimensional Euclidean item region, with nonnegative integrable valuations and positive total valuations and allocated utilities, has no supporting nonnegative integrable price at any nonnegative budgets. This negates the entire quantified Prove2Me continuum second-welfare statement.

counterexample.item_region: Closed unit ball in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1), with restricted volume; coordinate t.
counterexample.demand_space: All nonnegative essentially bounded bundles affordable at the integrable price; no individual upper supply cap.
counterexample.budgets: All nonnegative budget vectors, including zero coordinates.

limitations: Exact formal conclusion is the full negation of the platform statement; correspondence to the pinned preprint is documented separately.
Does not establish that every result in the paper is false, or refute its separate sorted globally linear-valuation characterization.
Prices are nonnegative L1 functions and demand uses the full nonnegative L-infinity cone; modified capped demand or other price spaces are different claims.
No repaired welfare theorem, downstream closure, exhaustive priority search, source-author endorsement or independent human proof review is claimed.
The written unit-interval normalization is explanatory and not a second separately kernel-checked target.
Verified third-party compiled caches remain trusted; this is not a Lean/Mathlib bootstrap verification.
